relevance_note: Kinetic study of five named LCAT-deficient probands (one classic, four Fish-eye disease), four with printed LCAT mutations: "a total of five patients with LCAT deficiency, one with classic LCAT deficiency and four with Fish-eye disease".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script assembled the JSON and sliced table-row spans from the Markdown lines, and every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Labels: the text calls the patients 'no. 1'...'no. 5' (Tables I-IV use the same numbers under 'Subjects'), so rule 1 gives 'no. n'. The older brother of no. 1 (LCAT deficiency, renal failure at 28 yr with dialysis) is a relative row. Table I is garbled in conversion: the first data row reads 'I Partial LCAT deficiency' (the patient number 1 merged with the 'Partial LCAT deficiency' subheading); its values (creatinine 1.9, urine protein 5.7 g/d) match the text's description of no. 1, so it was read as no. 1. Table I 'Age' (header unit yr) was taken as age at the study (last evaluation). No. 1's molecular defect 'has not been established': no variant row. Variant strings are copied as printed including OCR damage ('Met2s2 to Lys', 'deletion of Leuzoo'); the true residue numbers are not recoverable from the text and were not inferred. Variant type for the Leu deletion left 'not reported' (the authors call it only 'a deletion'). Nos. 3 and 4 are siblings 'diagnosed at the ages of 53 and 49 yr' without 'respectively'; ages at diagnosis were not assigned by position. 'Requiring corneal transplant in one' does not say which sibling, so treatment left not reported for both. Low HDL cholesterol and low apoA-I/apoA-II were recorded from each patient's Table II row against the control row (n=30, mean and SD in the same table), plus the text for no. 2. Triglycerides: elevated is stated only for the complete-deficient patient (no. 1); for the partial patients the text says 'variably elevated' and the Discussion says 'three of the patients we studied had normal plasma triglyceride levels' without naming them, so hypertriglyceridemia is not reported for nos. 2-5. 'No evidence of anemia or renal disease' for the named group of partial-deficient patients (nos. 2-5) was used to exclude anemia, nephrotic syndrome and CKD/renal failure (renal disease is broader); proteinuria and hematuria left not reported (urine protein '<0.5' g/d). 'Clinical evidence of coronary heart disease was absent in all five' and no coronary calcification (nos. 1, 3, 4) are recorded as excluded features, but the broader checklist item 'atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease' is left not reported (narrower absence). First author is not legible in the garbled author line, so it is 'not reported'. Prior reports: (36) renal histopathology of no. 1 and brother, (37) no. 2, (34) no. 5; nos. 3-4 are cited to (38) for their clinical history and (35) for the deletion. No. 2's genotype is attributed to 'H. Pritchard, unpublished data'. No contradictions found.
